title: {Syn} Perfect Numbers Follow Mersenne Prime Shadows
content:
A perfect number equals the sum of its positive divisors excluding itself. The first example is 6, because 1 + 2 + 3 equals 6.

Euclid and Euler showed that every even perfect number has the form 2^(p-1)(2^p - 1) where 2^p - 1 is prime. No odd perfect number is known.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
